trust_decision.summary: PROVENANCE MISMATCH. The advisory names mov_read_ispe() (HEIF ispe uint32 -> int), but at the pinned commit mov_read_ispe already rejects 0 and >INT_MAX before storing. The listed fix commit changes something unrelated: in the muxer helper ff_reshuffle_raw_rgb() (libavformat/rawutils.c), stride/size products are computed from codecpar width/height/bits_per_coded_sample before a raw RGB packet is reallocated and copied, and the fix bounds them against INT_MAX.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names mov_read_ispe in libavformat/mov.c. That spot is already guarded at the pinned commit (libavformat/mov.c:9577), so the summary leads away from the code the fix actually changes.

fix_sites.entry_point: muxing raw RGB video via avformat_write_header/av_write_frame into AVI (libavformat/avienc.c:794) or MOV unaligned QT RGB (libavformat/movenc.c:7692), e.g. ffmpeg CLI -c:v rawvideo -f avi/mov

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Callers compute expected_stride as int from an int64 expression (libavformat/avienc.c:793, libavformat/movenc.c:7691). A solver could argue the callers' narrowing is not the helper's problem, since the helper is the only place the fix touched.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: PAL8 raw frames carrying a trailing 1024-byte palette (contains_pal) and padded-stride reshuffling must keep working for normal sizes. A fix that rejects every size mismatch or pkt->size != expected size would break AVI/MOV raw RGB and PAL8 muxing.

O6_input_shapes: bits_per_coded_sample 15 mapped to 16, other bpc used directly (libavformat/rawutils.c:31)
packet with appended palette vs without (libavformat/rawutils.c:33-35)
expected_stride from the AVI 4-byte alignment vs the MOV 2-byte alignment caller

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The callers narrow an int64 stride expression to int expected_stride before passing it in; the fix only rejects expected_stride <= 0 and does not guard the caller-side narrowing.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The caller is outside the fixed file, and the helper's new <=0 check catches some of the wrapped values.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 1 file from fix site, same package

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Same caller-side int narrowing of expected_stride on the MOV unaligned QT RGB path.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Only used for the legacy QuickTime RGB mode (is_unaligned_qt_rgb).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 1 file from fix site, same package

O8b_injection_room.sibling: HEIF grid output width/height are read as uint32 (avio_rb32) into the tile_grid fields with no INT_MAX check, unlike ispe.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is the advisory's own uint32->int theme. The ispe check at libavformat/mov.c:9577 was not mirrored onto the grid/iovl header reads (also libavformat/mov.c:10714-10715).

O9_family: integer overflow / signed narrowing in size and stride arithmetic (CWE-190)

O10_build.project_tests: FATE (make fate); tests/fate/avformat.mak and the lavf rawvideo/avi/mov muxing tests. HEIF demux tests are in tests/fate/mov.mak (not opened).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Following the advisory text: add an INT_MAX check to mov_read_ispe, which is already present, and leave rawutils.c untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: Advisory text vs fix commit mismatch: the advisory describes mov_read_ispe, but the fix commit is avformat/rawutils. Either the fix commit or the summary is mis-attributed; the candidate record should be re-checked upstream before use.
